message.reasoning_content: We need to determine the crime(s) for the described case. The facts: a public official (谢某某) working at the housing registration center (房产局房屋登记中心) accepted a call from a private person (谢1某) to facilitate fraudulent issuance of a property title (房产证) using forged land certificates and planning permits. He processed the application without proper verification, resulting in issuance of a false property certificate, which was then used to obtain mortgage loans and credit cards, leading to fraud and large losses. The official's conduct: abuse of power, dereliction of duty, facilitating fraud. The charge likely is "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) or "徇私舞弊罪" (accepting bribes? Not bribery, but collusion). In Chinese criminal law, there is a crime "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of official duties to commit fraud) under Article 395 of Criminal Law (now 2021). It covers officials who, in the performance of duties, accept bribes or collude to issue false certificates, causing losses. Also "受贿罪" if bribe, but here he was asked to give favor, maybe no bribe? The facts: 谢1某 gave a phone call to 谢某某, asking for help. No mention of money given to official. So not bribery. The official simply failed to verify documents, facilitating fraud. That is "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of official duties). Also possibly "职务侵占"? No, not appropriation. So answer: 徇私舞弊罪. In examples, they sometimes list "滥用职权" as separate. The public official's crime: "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) or "徇私舞弊罪". The description: "对本职工作严重不负责任，不履行或不正确履行自己的工作职责，致使公共财产、国家和人民利益遭受重大损失" matches "徇私舞弊罪". So answer: [罪名]徇私舞弊罪<eoa>
